description:
Issue mutations commit through one redo record over the files they write, so a mutation's cost scales with what it changes instead of with the event log and the whole repository. The rollback transaction kernel and the phased repository capture it depends on are removed, leaving the storage layer smaller than it is now.

## Background

A jit mutation serializes on the repository lock, captures a closed image of the repository, derives its changes, and publishes them through a journaled transaction kernel. That kernel stages new bytes, backs up old files, records expected preimages and final identities, verifies each target several times against its SHA-256 digest, and can roll back or recover a partially published change. Every mutation also rewrites the whole event log as a file replacement. The event log is 3 MB in this repository and grows with project history, so the cost of each mutation grows with it.

Capture reads the registries, the event log, and every issue file, and hashes each one. It then reads them again in each later capture phase, and once more at apply to revalidate the whole read set. Profiling a label update on an 876-issue adopter repository after the capture-scoping work shows three dominant costs: SHA-256 over captured and published bytes, about a third of the time; parsing every issue; and publishing the event log, which is re-read and re-hashed about eight times.

`@/charter/D-17` replaces this mechanism. The repository lock serializes jit writers. Before commit, a mutation compares the live bytes of each file it writes with the bytes it read, and checks the event log's length and tail. Its commit point is one synced redo record under the data root's gitignored `tmp/`, holding the new bytes and mode of each written file, each deleted path, and the event append as an offset and bytes, over data-root and worktree paths. Applying the record replaces each file by temp-file and rename, removes each deleted path, and writes the append in place. Opening a session replays a leftover record. The decision supersedes decisions D11 and D14 of the archived transactional-materialization plan `cdc840ad`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A label update completes in under 100 ms wall time, as the median of three runs, on a tmpfs copy of the adopter-scale repository and on this repository. The evidence is a committed benchmark artifact reporting before and after for a changing label update, an idempotent label update, and a lease-refused update.
- [hard] REQ-02: A label update's median wall time on a repository whose event log is ten times larger differs by less than 10 % from the same update on the original repository.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every repository mutation publishes through one redo record. An interruption injected at every step of publication and recovery leaves the complete old state, or, after the next session opens, the complete new state, on both storage backends.
- [hard] REQ-04: A mutation whose written file, or whose event-log length or tail, changed after it was read returns a retryable conflict and changes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-05: No rollback kernel, transaction backup, staging directory, reverse action, worktree companion, apply-time revalidation of the whole read set, plan hash over captured entries, phased capture, listing fingerprint, or mutation document closure remains, and no second publication path exists beside the redo record. The one exception is `jit init`, which creates an absent data root through a stage directory and a no-replace rename.
- [hard] REQ-06: The epic's cumulative diff from `34d37f8be` removes more lines than it adds across the Rust workspace, counting production code and tests.
- [hard] REQ-07: The project invariants, the storage-format reference, and every document describing mutation publication or recovery state the redo-record mechanism, and none describes journaled rollback.

## Notes

- Moved here from `9750b151`, whose capture-scoping work took the adopter-repository label update from 1.8 s to 110 ms: its 100 ms criterion, now REQ-01.
- `jit init` publishes through the kernel today and has no publication code of its own. It keeps synced staging and no-replace rename (`@/inv/atomic-writes`) in a small init-only publisher without a journal, and writes the data root's `.gitignore` naming `tmp/`.
- The record carries make-directory, put, delete, and event-append operations over data-root and worktree paths. The make-directory operation was added during execution (ESC-09), because the three-operation form had no representation for the empty directory a tree export creates. `plan_hash`, `transaction_id`, and `transaction_cleanup_pending` leave the profile commands' JSON output.
- The investigation linked to the planning issue maps each REQ-05 term to the construct it names.
- The intake brief linked to this issue carries the measurements, profiles, code inventory, owner decisions, and open questions for planning.
title: Mutations commit through a redo record and never scale with project history
